items.title: Reversible thermodynamic process record
items.statement:
Let $P=(I_P,x_P^-,x_P^+,z_P,\kappa_P,r_P)$ be an admitted closed process record as defined in [[def-td-process-and-protocol]], with equilibrium endpoints $x_P^-,x_P^+\in D_c$. The record is **reversible relative to its declared boundary and protocol** when the model also admits a reverse record $P^{\mathrm{rev}}$ for the same system and material constitution, starting at $x_P^+$ and ending at $x_P^-$, such that every auxiliary and device state specified by the protocol is restored to its initial state and every signed boundary transfer is reversed. In particular,

$$Q[P^{\mathrm{rev}}]=-Q[P],\qquad W_{\mathrm{on}}[P^{\mathrm{rev}}]=-W_{\mathrm{on}}[P].$$

If the protocol records additional transfer channels, their signed values must likewise be negatives of their forward values. A record that is slow is not reversible merely because it is slow; it must satisfy the reverse-record condition above. Reversibility is therefore relative to what the model includes inside the boundary and which reverse controls it admits.

David Tong, Statistical Physics, Chapter 4 of the complete author-hosted lecture notes, §§4.3.1–4.3.4
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§2.5–2.6

items.physical_scope: Admitted closed process records with equilibrium endpoints in the nonrelativistic macroscopic thermodynamic framework; reversibility is relative to the declared system, auxiliary-device boundary, and transfer protocol.

items.title: Thermal contact family and constraints
items.statement:
For each material constitution $c$, let $D_c$ be the equilibrium state domain from [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. A **thermal-contact family** is a model-declared set $\mathcal T$ of tagged pairs $a=(c_A,x_A)$ with $x_A\in D_{c_A}$. Its tag and coordinate projections are $\operatorname{tag}(a)=c_A$ and $\operatorname{coord}(a)=x_A$; equal numerical coordinate tuples with different constitution tags are not identified.

Fix two members $a=(c_A,x_A)$ and $b=(c_B,x_B)$, named constituents $A,B$ of those constitutions, and a declared contact-protocol convention. A **thermal-contact protocol** is an admitted preparation/process record $P$ of their compound system $A\sqcup B$, with the configuration curve $z_P:I_P\to Z_{A\sqcup B}$ and equilibrium endpoint configurations specified in [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]. The contact model supplies constituent endpoint-coordinate maps

$$\xi_A:Z_{A\sqcup B}^{\mathrm{eq}}\to D_{c_A},\qquad \xi_B:Z_{A\sqcup B}^{\mathrm{eq}}\to D_{c_B},$$

and requires $\xi_A(z_P(t_0))=x_A$ and $\xi_B(z_P(t_0))=x_B$. These constituent maps are additional declared model data; they are not inferred from the compound's coordinate tuple. Write $x_A^+=\xi_A(z_P(t_1))$ and $x_B^+=\xi_B(z_P(t_1))$ for the constituent final coordinates. The two constituents are separated by a declared diathermal contact: matter transfer and mechanical or composition work across that contact are forbidden, while the protocol permits thermal energy transfer between the constituents. The compound's external boundary and all retained constraints are specified as in [[def-td-system-and-permitted-exchanges]] and [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]. No continuity or differentiability of the configuration curve is added here.

Let $\mathcal P_T(A,B)$ be the set of contact records admitted by the fixed convention. The model supplies an internal transfer map $q_{A\to B}:\mathcal P_T(A,B)\to\mathbb R$, whose values are numerical magnitudes in joules: $q_{A\to B}[P]>0$ means net thermal energy transferred from $A$ to $B$ across this contact during $I_P$. Set $q_{B\to A}[P]:=-q_{A\to B}[P]$. Zero net internal heat transfer means exactly $q_{A\to B}[P]=0$; it does not assert zero transfer at every intermediate time. This map is additional protocol data, distinct from the compound's external-boundary map $Q$ in [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]. In particular, an isolated compound may have nonzero $q_{A\to B}$ while its external $Q$ is zero. Identifying this internal map with constituent heat records requires separately supplied constituent records and consistent boundary assignments.

For each tested ordered pair $(a,b)$, the convention specifies one admitted contact preparation $P_{a,b}\in\mathcal P_T(A,B)$ with the initial coordinates above, and a subset $\mathcal E_T(A,B)\subseteq\mathcal P_T(A,B)$ designated as equilibrium contact preparations. These are model inputs, not an equilibration theorem. The pair is in **thermal contact equilibrium**, written $a\sim_T b$, exactly when its selected record $P_{a,b}$ belongs to $\mathcal E_T(A,B)$, has $x_A^+=x_A$ and $x_B^+=x_B$, and satisfies $q_{A\to B}[P_{a,b}]=0$. Untested pairs are not in the relation. This criterion is protocol-dependent: changing the selected preparation or retained constraints can change the relation. For fixed constitutions, coordinate notation $x_A\sim_T x_B$ abbreviates $(c_A,x_A)\sim_T(c_B,x_B)$ using the two specified tag embeddings. It does not define a relation on untagged coordinates across unspecified material types. The relation is defined only on the stated family $\mathcal T$ and for the declared contact protocols. This definition does not assert that $\sim_T$ is reflexive, symmetric, or transitive, and it does not assign a real-valued temperature to its equivalence classes. Lieb–Yngvason §IV.A instead defines thermal equilibrium using adiabatic equivalence with a thermal join; the present record-based criterion is a separately adopted convention.

items.physical_scope: Admitted pair contacts between equilibrium macrostates of the nonrelativistic macroscopic thermodynamic framework; no temperature scale or contact transitivity is defined here.

items.title: Concave macroscopic fundamental entropy
items.statement:
For each admitted material constitution $c$, the model adopts a finite scalar function

$$S_c:D_c\longrightarrow\mathbb R\ \text{with values measured in }\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}},$$

on the equilibrium state domain $D_c$ of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. This framework treats $S_c$ as primitive constitutive data: its existence and form are assumed, not derived from the word entropy, statistical mechanics, or experimental evidence.

On every specified convex region $C\subseteq D_c$ in the dimensionless coordinates of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]], $S_c$ is continuous and concave, meaning that for all $x,y\in C$ and every $\alpha\in[0,1]$ ([[def-interval]]),

$$S_c((1-\alpha)x+\alpha y)\ge (1-\alpha)S_c(x)+\alpha S_c(y).$$

The domain assumptions are local to the material and region named; no unlisted coordinate tuple is presumed physically realizable. The input of $S_c$ is the represented state $\pi_c(e)$; when the function is written using physical coordinates $(U,V,n_1,\ldots,n_r)$, those coordinates mean the SI values whose dimensionless numerical tuple is $\pi_c(e)$. For independent separated macroscopic systems $A,B$ admitted by [[post-td-bulk-additivity]], entropy is additive under that postulate's composition map $\kappa_{AB}$:

$$S_{A\sqcup B}(\kappa_{AB}(x_A,x_B))=S_A(x_A)+S_B(x_B).$$

On each separately designated open, single-phase chart in the physical coordinates $(U,V,n_1,\ldots,n_r)$, assume the numerical representative of $S_c$ is $C^2$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]: its first and second coordinate partial derivatives exist and are continuous. The partial derivative $S_U$ at fixed $V,n_1,\ldots,n_r$ is the ordinary partial derivative in the $U$ coordinate, as in [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], and is assumed finite and strictly positive. The numerical chart input uses $\hat U=U/(1\,\mathrm J)$; consequently $S_U=(1\,\mathrm J)^{-1}\partial S_c/\partial\hat U$ and has units $\mathrm{K^{-1}}$. The other physical coordinates are similarly represented using the fixed SI units of [[def-td-si-quantities]]. No differentiability, strict concavity, or positive $S_U$ is asserted outside those charts. This item does not itself define a thermometer calibration or claim a temperature law.

For the tagged bulk family with scaling maps $\delta_\lambda$ and domains $B_{c,\lambda}$ from [[post-td-bulk-additivity]], also adopt, for every admitted $\lambda>0$ and $x\in B_{c,\lambda}$,

$$S_{c^{(\lambda)}}(\delta_\lambda x)=\lambda S_c(x).$$

This is a bulk homogeneity assumption for tagged scaled systems, not exact finite-size scaling for every body. Lieb–Yngvason develop a different accessibility-based route in which entropy is represented from additional operational hypotheses; this framework does not claim that their derivation proves the present primitive entropy postulate.

items.physical_scope: The adopted entropy representation for the declared nonrelativistic, macroscopic, additive bulk thermodynamic systems; smooth derivative conditions apply only on the named single-phase charts.

items.title: Isolated compound and feasible equilibrium set
items.statement:
Fix a finite list of named subsystems $s_1,\ldots,s_m$, where $m\in\mathbb N$ and $m\ge1$ ([[def-natural-numbers]]), each having its own equilibrium state domain $D_{c_i}$ as defined in [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. Their separated endpoint state space is the Cartesian product ([[def-cartesian-product]])

$$\mathcal D:=D_{c_1}\times\cdots\times D_{c_m}.$$

If the boundary also includes named auxiliaries or work devices $d_1,\ldots,d_k$ not already among the $s_i$, where $k\in\mathbb N$, supply endpoint state sets $Y_j$ and energy maps $E_j:Y_j\to\mathbb R$ with numerical values interpreted in joules. Supply also every coordinate map needed for their matter, volume, retained constraints and separately tracked mechanical or external-field energy. The complete endpoint space is

$$\mathcal D_{\mathrm{all}}:=\mathcal D\times Y_1\times\cdots\times Y_k.$$

For $k=0$ use $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{all}}=\mathcal D$. Write an endpoint as $(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)$ and obtain constituent states by coordinate projection. In the separated additive energy model, declare $E_{\mathrm{tot}}(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)=\sum_{i=1}^{m}U_{c_i}(x_i)+\sum_{j=1}^{k}E_j(y_j)\,\mathrm J$, with finite sums as in [[def-finite-sum]] and the empty auxiliary sum zero. Every tracked endpoint energy contribution must be included in these maps or in an additional explicitly supplied contribution; an interacting model must supply its total-energy map on $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{all}}$. For each entropy-bearing auxiliary supply $S_j^{\mathrm{aux}}:Y_j\to\mathbb R$ with values in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. If the complete separated split has an adopted additive entropy model, its total includes those maps as well as the $S_{c_i}$; omitting an auxiliary requires an explicitly constant entropy contribution or a supplied reduced total-entropy function.

An **isolated compound** consists of all these constituents inside a declared outer boundary, with no matter or energy transfer across that boundary during the admitted process, in the sense of [[def-td-system-and-permitted-exchanges]]. Internal transfers may change auxiliary energy and entropy. On pairs admitted to the simple aggregate composition map of [[post-td-bulk-additivity]], totals and entropy satisfy that postulate and [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]]. A retained partition endpoint in $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{all}}$ is not automatically such an admitted aggregate state: summing its coordinates can discard partition information. For endpoints outside that composition's admitted set, total-energy and total-entropy maps must be supplied separately; no aggregate entropy identity is inferred.

For specified totals and retained barriers, an **equilibrium feasible set** is the model-declared subset $\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal D_{\mathrm{all}}$ of complete endpoint tuples satisfying those totals and exactly the exchange permissions in the declared protocol. Its thermodynamic projection is $\Pi(\mathcal F):=\{\mathbf x\in\mathcal D:\exists\mathbf y\text{ with }(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)\in\mathcal F\}$; that projection alone does not record variable auxiliary states, energy or entropy. When $k=0$ the original convention $\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal D$ applies. Totals use all supplied endpoint maps and the dimensioned coordinate maps $U_c,V_c,n_{c,j}$ of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]], rather than treating numerical coordinates as quantities with units. For two constituents without auxiliaries, thermal contact through [[def-td-thermal-contact-constraints]] at fixed volumes and mole amounts gives the model-declared allowed energy partitions with prescribed total energy and any further retained constraints. Volume or species exchange changes $\mathcal F$ only when explicitly permitted; retained walls fix the corresponding coordinates.

The set $\mathcal F$ may be empty, noncompact, or otherwise fail to contain an entropy-maximizing state. This definition imposes no existence, compactness, convexity, uniqueness, or attainment assumption.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, Chapter 4 of the complete author-hosted lecture notes, §§4.1 and 4.3.3
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§2.2, 2.6 and 2.9

items.physical_scope: Feasible endpoint macrostates for a declared isolated compound of nonrelativistic macroscopic thermodynamic systems; only explicitly permitted exchanges and retained constraints are included.

items.title: Stable equilibrium requires an attained global entropy maximum
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal F$ be the explicitly declared feasible endpoint set of an isolated compound with the chosen independent separated macroscopic subsystem split and any explicitly modeled named auxiliaries, as defined in [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]. For this route, adopt the physical criterion that any endpoint tuple the model classifies as a stable equilibrium under these fixed totals, retained partitions, and permitted exchanges satisfies

$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x^{\mathrm{eq}})=\max_{x\in\mathcal F}S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x),\qquad S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x):=\sum_{i=1}^{m}S_{c_i}(x_i)+\sum_{j=1}^{k}S_j^{\mathrm{aux}}(y_j),$$

Here $\max$ means that $x^{\mathrm{eq}}\in\mathcal F$ and $S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x^{\mathrm{eq}})\ge S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x)$ for every $x\in\mathcal F$, using maximum in the sense of [[def-max-min]]. Here $x=(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)$ is a complete endpoint tuple from [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]; $k=0$ gives the original thermodynamic-only formula. The finite sums are as in [[def-finite-sum]]. The macroscopic summands are those of the separated constituents under [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]], and any auxiliary summands are the explicitly adopted endpoint entropy maps of the same complete compound model. This route assumes that these contributions add for the complete admitted split. A constant auxiliary entropy may be dropped as an additive constant when comparing maxima, whereas variable auxiliary entropy must be retained. Whenever the stable-equilibrium label is used, attainment is assumed: at least one maximizing endpoint lies in $\mathcal F$. If $\mathcal F$ is empty or the entropy supremum is not attained, this item supplies no equilibrium state.

“Global” refers to every endpoint in this exact $\mathcal F$, not just nearby states, states reachable by a restricted short-time dynamics, or states on a selected branch. A local maximum that is not global, or a long-lived preparation trapped by kinetic barriers, is not declared stable equilibrium by this postulate. No uniqueness or relaxation dynamics is assumed.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, Chapter 4 of the complete author-hosted lecture notes, §§4.3.3–4.3.4
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §2.9

items.physical_scope: Global stable equilibrium of an explicitly specified isolated macroscopic compound under its stated total-coordinate constraints and permitted exchanges; no claim about local maxima or dynamical relaxation is included.

items.title: Macroscopic second law for isolated compounds
items.statement:
For every admitted closed process record $P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)$ of an isolated compound, assume its declared outer boundary is isolated throughout, its material constitution is fixed, its center-of-mass kinetic and separately tracked external-field potential energies have zero endpoint change, and both endpoint preparations are equilibrium macrostates. Include every named auxiliary and work device in the compound. Fix the finite constituent split $s_1,\ldots,s_m$ used for the endpoint bookkeeping, with $m\in\mathbb N$, $m\ge1$, and constitutions $c_1,\ldots,c_m$. Every additional named auxiliary or work device has an endpoint set $Y_j$, energy map, and adopted entropy map $S_j^{\mathrm{aux}}$ as in [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]. Every constituent whose entropy can change must occur either in the thermodynamic split or through one of these explicit auxiliary maps. Every auxiliary is retained in the complete endpoint tuples and energy constraints. An explicitly entropy-neutral device may be assigned $S_j^{\mathrm{aux}}=0$; more generally an auxiliary with declared zero endpoint entropy change cancels in the displayed inequality, while its variable state and energy remain in $\mathcal F$. Its endpoint product is

$$\mathcal D_{\mathrm{all}}:=(D_{c_1}\times\cdots\times D_{c_m})\times Y_1\times\cdots\times Y_k,\qquad \mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal D_{\mathrm{all}},$$

where $\mathcal F$ is the model-declared feasible endpoint set for the fixed totals, retained barriers, and permitted exchanges, as in [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]. The process model supplies an endpoint association on the two formal endpoint labels $-$ and $+$:

$$\rho_P:\{-,+\}\longrightarrow\mathcal F,\qquad \rho_P(-)=\mathbf x_P^-=(x_{1,P}^-,\ldots,x_{m,P}^-,y_{1,P}^-,\ldots,y_{k,P}^-),\qquad \rho_P(+)=\mathbf x_P^+=(x_{1,P}^+,\ldots,x_{m,P}^+,y_{1,P}^+,\ldots,y_{k,P}^+),$$

where $\mathbf x_P^-$ and $\mathbf x_P^+$ are respectively the declared constituent-state tuples including all auxiliary endpoint states and representing the aggregate equilibrium endpoints $x_P^-$ and $x_P^+$ of $P$. Both tuples must belong to the same $\mathcal F$. Restrict to endpoint splits admitted by [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]] as a collection of independent separated macroscopic systems, so that its additive entropy rule applies to the macroscopic split; additionally adopt additivity of the explicitly modeled auxiliary entropy contributions for the complete compound. For $k=0$ this is the original thermodynamic-only split. On this admitted $\mathcal F$, define

$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}(\mathbf x):=\sum_{i=1}^{m}S_{c_i}(x_i)+\sum_{j=1}^{k}S_j^{\mathrm{aux}}(y_j)\qquad\left(\mathbf x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m,y_1,\ldots,y_k)\in\mathcal F\right).$$

This uses the finite-sum convention of [[def-finite-sum]].

The adopted macroscopic second law is

$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}(\rho_P(+))-S_{\mathrm{tot}}(\rho_P(-))\ge0.$$

The process record and the zero-change conditions are those of [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]. The process may pass through nonequilibrium configurations; this postulate compares endpoint entropies only and assigns no entropy function to those intermediate configurations.

For an admitted reversible operation in the sense of [[def-td-reversible-process]], adopt $S_{\mathrm{tot}}(\rho_P(+))-S_{\mathrm{tot}}(\rho_P(-))=0$. An admitted irreversible adiabatic operation may have a strictly positive entropy increase, but strict increase is not required for every irreversible operation. The postulate does not state monotonicity for an open compound, an externally driven process, a subsystem that exchanges energy with an omitted environment, or every microscopic trajectory.

items.title: Zeroth law for the declared thermal-contact family
items.statement:
For the declared thermal-contact family $\mathcal T$ and the contact relation $\sim_T$ of [[def-td-thermal-contact-constraints]], assume that $\sim_T$ is an equivalence relation: for all $x,y,z\in\mathcal T$,

$$x\sim_T x,\qquad x\sim_T y\Longrightarrow y\sim_T x,\qquad x\sim_T y\ \text{and}\ y\sim_T z\Longrightarrow x\sim_T z.$$

This is an adopted physical assumption about the stated contact protocols. It does not by itself construct a real-valued thermometer reading, an absolute temperature, a differentiable temperature state function, or a common calibration across different material families. Those require further operational, entropy, regularity, and calibration hypotheses.

items.title: Common constitutive entropy law for a designated bulk family
items.physical_scope: A separately designated nonrelativistic macroscopic bulk branch of a fixed material law, with fixed species and intensive constitutive parameters, common SI and energy/entropy reference conventions, and omitted interface, surface and long-range interaction terms; exact finite-body or arbitrary gravitating-system extensivity is not asserted.
items.statement:
In addition to the general tagged bulk family of [[post-td-bulk-additivity]] and its entropy law in [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]], designate a common-constitutive-law bulk branch as follows. Fix a material constitution $c$ with an ordered species list and fixed intensive constitutive parameters. Let $C\subseteq D_c$ be a nonempty open single-phase chart in the fixed dimensionless SI numerical coordinates of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]] and [[def-td-si-quantities]], and assume it is a positive cone: $\lambda x\in C$ for all $x\in C$ and $\lambda>0$. Use the adopted $C^2$ entropy with $S_{c,U}>0$ on this chart.

For every $\lambda>0$, admit scaling of every $x\in C$, so $C\subseteq B_{c,\lambda}$, and retain the distinct scaled-system tag $c^{(\lambda)}$. The image $C^{(\lambda)}:=\delta_\lambda(C)$ is a chart in $D_{c^{(\lambda)}}$. Adopt a coordinate-preserving material-law transport $j_{c,\lambda}:C^{(\lambda)}\to C$ defined in numerical coordinates by $j_{c,\lambda}(y)=y$, and adopt entropy preservation under that transport:

$$S_{c^{(\lambda)}}(y)=S_c(j_{c,\lambda}(y))\qquad(y\in C^{(\lambda)}).$$

The transport identifies the constitutive numerical law used for bodies in this branch; it does not equate their physical identities or material tags. It presumes a common ordered species list, units, internal-energy reference and entropy calibration. Fixed material parameters in this branch exclude a hidden size parameter whose independent variation changes the law. Combined with the existing tagged entropy law, this adopted transport gives the same-function relation

$$S_c(\lambda x)=S_{c^{(\lambda)}}(\delta_\lambda x)=\lambda S_c(x)\qquad(x\in C,\ \lambda>0).$$

This is additional idealized constitutive information for the designated bulk branch. It is not implied by coordinate additivity, SI units, the general tagged relation, or the existence of local equilibrium charts. No empirical proof, finite-size error bound, or assertion for surface-sensitive, interacting long-range or self-gravitating bodies is supplied. Euler and Gibbs–Duhem identities are conditional deductions on this branch, not part of the postulate's source review.

references.title: Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, Chapter 2, section 2.6.4 and equations 2.103–2.112

items.title: Entropy increase in an idealized adiabatic compression
items.statement:
This is a conditional model calculation, not a report of an observed compression. The gas is taken to have one mole, $n=1\,\mathrm{mol}$, of a model whose state variables are a positive temperature $T$ in kelvins, volume $V$ in cubic metres, and uniform pressure $p$ in pascals. The model is monatomic and ideal in the explicit sense that its molar constant-volume heat capacity is $C_V=3R/2$, its internal energy is $U=nC_VT$, and its equation of state is $pV=nRT$. Its entropy difference is

$$S(T,V)-S(T_0,V_0)=nC_V\ln(T/T_0)+nR\ln(V/V_0),$$

for positive reference values $T_0$ in K and $V_0$ in $\mathrm{m^3}$. At initial equilibrium let $T_i>0$ and $V_i>0$. A piston protocol suddenly raises the external pressure from the initial value $p_i$ to a constant final load $p_f$, compresses the gas adiabatically to $V_f=(9/10)V_i$, and dissipatively settles it to a final equilibrium state. The protocol admits no reverse record, so it is irreversible by [[def-td-reversible-process]]. The idealization assumes no change in the included load's entropy; all numerical behavior is a model assumption and deduction, not an empirical measurement.

references.title: Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §2.6, ideal-gas entropy and adiabatic examples
David Tong, Statistical Physics, Chapter 4 of the complete author-hosted lecture notes, §§4.3.3–4.3.4
Lieb and Yngvason, The Physics and Mathematics of the Second Law of Thermodynamics, §§II.F and IV.A

items.strategy: Direct conditional derivation from the stated ideal-gas constitutive model, admitted process/work protocol, first-law postulate, and exact logarithm laws.
items.physical_scope: A conditional one-mole monatomic ideal-gas model with positive initial temperature and volume, a sudden constant-load compression to a stated final volume, dissipative settling, and no empirical claim.

items.title: A concave entropy supremum not attained on an open energy-partition set
items.statement:
Take two independent separated one-species systems $A$ and $B$ with material constitutions $c_A,c_B$ inside an isolated compound. Write $D_A:=D_{c_A}$ and $D_B:=D_{c_B}$ for their equilibrium domains; each is $(0,\infty)^3$ in the dimensionless coordinates $(\hat U_i,\hat V_i,\hat n_i)$ of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]], and each full domain is designated as an open single-phase chart. Fix positive volumes and amounts $\hat V_A,\hat V_B,\hat n_A,\hat n_B$, total internal energy $U_A+U_B=1\,\mathrm J$, and a thermal-contact protocol that permits internal energy transfer while keeping volumes and amounts fixed, as in [[def-td-thermal-contact-constraints]]. Adopt the retained product endpoint set and the separately specified total maps below:

$$\phi(x)=((x,\hat V_A,\hat n_A),(1-x,\hat V_B,\hat n_B)),\qquad \mathcal F=\{\phi(x):0<x<1\}\subseteq D_A\times D_B.$$

Thus $x=\hat U_A=U_A/(1\,\mathrm J)$ and $1-x=\hat U_B=U_B/(1\,\mathrm J)$. With $s_*=1\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, adopt the toy constitutive entropies $S_A=2s_*\hat U_A$ and $S_B=s_*\hat U_B$. They are finite, continuous, affine (hence concave), $C^2$, and have positive $S_U$ on the stated open domains. For each $\lambda>0$, use the same formula in the own coordinates of the distinct tags $c_A^{(\lambda)}$ and $c_B^{(\lambda)}$. Then the coordinate scaling $\delta_\lambda$ of [[post-td-bulk-additivity]] gives $S_{c_A^{(\lambda)}}(\delta_\lambda x_A)=\lambda S_A(x_A)$ and $S_{c_B^{(\lambda)}}(\delta_\lambda x_B)=\lambda S_B(x_B)$. Adopt $S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x_A,x_B):=S_A(x_A)+S_B(x_B)$ as additional entropy data on the retained product endpoints, independently of simple aggregate composition. Its value on $\mathcal F$ is $S_{\mathrm{tot}}(\phi(x))=s_*(1+x)$. The model-declared feasible set is an open energy-partition interval, so its entropy has a finite supremum but no attained maximum. This is a conditional model example, not a claim about a real material.

For complete contact data, set $E:=(0,1)$ and take $Z_{A\sqcup B}=Z_{A\sqcup B}^{\mathrm{eq}}=\mathcal F$, with constituent maps $\xi_A,\xi_B$ the two coordinate projections and contact family $\mathcal T:=\{(c_A,x_A):x_A\in D_A\}\cup\{(c_B,x_B):x_B\in D_B\}$. The two constitutions share one species label. Give the aggregate constitution the domain $D_{A\sqcup B}=(0,\infty)^3$, and set $\xi_{A\sqcup B}(\phi(x))=(1,\hat V_A+\hat V_B,\hat n_A+\hat n_B)$. This is a supplied aggregate coordinate map for process records, not an assertion of an aggregate entropy identity. For each $x,y\in E$ with $y\ge x$, admit the record $P_{x,y}$ of [[def-td-process-and-protocol]] on $I=[0,1]$ seconds: its aggregate endpoints are both this constant coordinate tuple, $z_{x,y}(t)=\phi(x)$ for $0\le t<1$ and $z_{x,y}(1)=\phi(y)$, its control record is $(x,y)$, and its signed transfer record is the real number $x-y$. Declare the control-record set to be $\{(x,y)\in E^2:y\ge x\}$ and the transfer-record set to be $\mathbb R$. No path regularity is required by the supplier. The outer boundary admits no matter or energy transfer; fixed constituent volumes and amounts and zero contact work are retained constraints. Supply fixed positive constituent and compound masses and zero endpoint center-of-mass velocities in one Galilean chart, and no separately tracked external-field energy. Thus these are core closed records, with $Q[P_{x,y}]=W_{\mathrm{on}}[P_{x,y}]=0$. For the contact-record set $\mathcal P_T=\{P_{x,y}:x,y\in E,\ y\ge x\}$ supply $q_{A\to B}[P_{x,y}]=x-y$ in joule magnitudes as in [[def-td-thermal-contact-constraints]]. The constituent energy changes are $(y-x)\,\mathrm J$ and $(x-y)\,\mathrm J$. Each feasible endpoint has its self-record; nonzero transfers occur when $y>x$. No contact-equilibrium designation or relaxation law is assumed.

To check consistency with the separately scoped aggregate postulates, take $\mathcal C_{AB}:=\{(x_A,x_B)\in D_A\times D_B:\hat U_A=\hat U_B\}$ and let $\kappa_{AB}$ sum their three coordinates. Adopt $S_{A\sqcup B}(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n)=\tfrac32s_*\hat U$. On this nonempty admission set, $S_A+S_B=3s_*\hat U_A=S_{A\sqcup B}(\kappa_{AB}(x_A,x_B))$, and all dimensioned coordinates add. Use the same aggregate formula on its scaled tags and all positive-coordinate scaling domains. Only the retained partition $x=1/2$ is in this aggregate admission set; there the product entropy and aggregate entropy both equal $3s_*/2$. All other retained partitions have separately adopted product entropy, so no aggregate entropy identity is asserted for them. Totals and entropy on these complete partitioned endpoints are additional declared maps allowed by [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]. The maximum criterion of [[post-td-entropy-maximum]] is used on their stated entropy sum; no aggregate-composition or accessibility theorem is claimed.

items.title: A local entropy maximum below a feasible global maximum
items.statement:
Take two independent separated one-species systems $A$ and $B$ with material constitutions $c_A,c_B$ inside an isolated compound. Write $D_A:=D_{c_A}$ and $D_B:=D_{c_B}$ for their equilibrium domains; each is $(0,\infty)^3$ in $(\hat U_i,\hat V_i,\hat n_i)$, and each full domain is designated as an open single-phase chart. Fix positive $\hat V_A,\hat V_B,\hat n_A,\hat n_B$, total energy $U_A+U_B=1\,\mathrm J$, $s_*=1\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, and toy entropies $S_A=2s_*\hat U_A$, $S_B=s_*\hat U_B$, using the same formulas on the distinct tagged constitutions $c_A^{(\lambda)}$ and $c_B^{(\lambda)}$ for every $\lambda>0$. Adopt the partitioned endpoint entropy $S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x_A,x_B):=S_A(x_A)+S_B(x_B)$ as additional model data and permit internal thermal energy transfer at fixed volumes and amounts by the explicit records below. This product entropy is not identified with a simple aggregate entropy after discarding the energy partition. Let

$$\phi(x)=((x,\hat V_A,\hat n_A),(1-x,\hat V_B,\hat n_B)),\qquad \mathcal F=\{\phi(x):x\in(0,3/10]\cup[3/5,9/10]\}.$$

The retained barrier constraint admits exactly this nonconvex subset of the energy partitions; all its pairs satisfy the same total energy, volume, and amount constraints. The additive entropy is $S_{\mathrm{tot}}(\phi(x))=s_*(1+x)$, so $x=3/10$ is a local maximum relative to $\mathcal F$ but lies below the feasible global maximum at $x=9/10$. These toy constitutive laws and constraints make no claim about a real material; calling an actual preparation metastable would require a separate kinetic model.

For complete contact data, set $E:=(0,3/10]\cup[3/5,9/10]$ and take $Z_{A\sqcup B}=Z_{A\sqcup B}^{\mathrm{eq}}=\mathcal F$, with constituent maps $\xi_A,\xi_B$ the two coordinate projections and contact family $\mathcal T:=\{(c_A,x_A):x_A\in D_A\}\cup\{(c_B,x_B):x_B\in D_B\}$. The two constitutions share one species label. Give the aggregate constitution the domain $D_{A\sqcup B}=(0,\infty)^3$, and set $\xi_{A\sqcup B}(\phi(x))=(1,\hat V_A+\hat V_B,\hat n_A+\hat n_B)$. This is a supplied aggregate coordinate map for process records, not an assertion of an aggregate entropy identity. For each $x,y\in E$ with $y\ge x$, admit the record $P_{x,y}$ of [[def-td-process-and-protocol]] on $I=[0,1]$ seconds: its aggregate endpoints are both this constant coordinate tuple, $z_{x,y}(t)=\phi(x)$ for $0\le t<1$ and $z_{x,y}(1)=\phi(y)$, its control record is $(x,y)$, and its signed transfer record is the real number $x-y$. Declare the control-record set to be $\{(x,y)\in E^2:y\ge x\}$ and the transfer-record set to be $\mathbb R$. No path regularity is required by the supplier. The outer boundary admits no matter or energy transfer; fixed constituent volumes and amounts and zero contact work are retained constraints. Supply fixed positive constituent and compound masses and zero endpoint center-of-mass velocities in one Galilean chart, and no separately tracked external-field energy. Thus these are core closed records, with $Q[P_{x,y}]=W_{\mathrm{on}}[P_{x,y}]=0$. For the contact-record set $\mathcal P_T=\{P_{x,y}:x,y\in E,\ y\ge x\}$ supply $q_{A\to B}[P_{x,y}]=x-y$ in joule magnitudes as in [[def-td-thermal-contact-constraints]]. The constituent energy changes are $(y-x)\,\mathrm J$ and $(x-y)\,\mathrm J$. Each feasible endpoint has its self-record; nonzero transfers occur when $y>x$. No contact-equilibrium designation or relaxation law is assumed.

To check consistency with the separately scoped aggregate postulates, take $\mathcal C_{AB}:=\{(x_A,x_B)\in D_A\times D_B:\hat U_A=\hat U_B\}$ and let $\kappa_{AB}$ sum their three coordinates. Adopt $S_{A\sqcup B}(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n)=\tfrac32s_*\hat U$. On this nonempty admission set, $S_A+S_B=3s_*\hat U_A=S_{A\sqcup B}(\kappa_{AB}(x_A,x_B))$, and all dimensioned coordinates add. Use the same aggregate formula on its scaled tags and all positive-coordinate scaling domains. The retained partitions in $\mathcal F$ have $x\ne1/2$ and are outside this aggregate admission set, so their separately adopted product entropy does not contradict the aggregate identity. Totals and entropy on these complete partitioned endpoints are additional declared maps allowed by [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]. The maximum criterion of [[post-td-entropy-maximum]] is used on their stated entropy sum; no aggregate-composition or accessibility theorem is claimed.
